title:
Comment of Jennifer Romig in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15424-000
Submission Date: 10/19/2026

documents.name: 151711.txt
documents.text:
Jennifer Romig, Missouri City, TX.
My name is Jennifer Romig, and I am deeply troubled by the real estate developer who wants to put an underwater data center in the Bay of Fundy off the coast of Maine. This area is critical habitat for endangered North Atlantic right whales. Tidal turbines, server hubs, increased sea vessel traffic, and underwater noise threaten the survival of these whales. Also at risk are fin whales, sturgeon, and other important marine species. I have traveled to Maine, and to see these creatures is an incredible gift, and we should all want to protect them.

The Bay of Fundy is a vital feeding area, nursery, and migratory corridor for the North Atlantic right whales. Did you know that this species is critically endangered? There are only about 350-380 left (data is from Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution). These beautiful creatures are slow-moving and often swim at the surface, making them highly susceptible to strikes from boats and other sea vessels. If data centers are allowed here, these precious whales could become tragic victims to the increased traffic.

Increased underwater noise from shipping, construction, and energy exploration disrupts their low-frequency calls, making it harder for them to find mates, communicate, or avoid danger. (This data is from NOAA.) How is an underwater data center going to improve these conditions? It won’t. There is already more than sufficient evidence showing that data centers on land cause severe noise pollution and constant stress for neighboring homes. Putting one underwater would be worse because underwater sound emissions from hardware and hard-drive vibrations can interfere with marine life that relies on natural ocean acoustics for communication and navigation. Also, sound travels 4.3 to 4.5 times faster and much farther underwater. The noise pollution would only be exacerbated underwater. (This data is from Nautil.us.)

There is a significant risk for thermal pollution. The heat generated by servers is discharged into the surrounding water (raising temperatures by roughly 1°C or more in localized areas). This extra warmth can disrupt breeding, feeding, and migration habits for marine species, and it adds stress to already warming ocean waters.

The pods and shells used to house underwater data centers require protective coatings to survive saltwater. Researchers and local communities in China where underwater data centers are being trialed have raised concerns that these chemical layers could flake off, dissolve into the sediment, or be ingested by fish and enter the food chain. The United States already has a severe problem with contamination in our seafood supplies. Seafood is vital for human cardiac health, not to mention sustaining the North Atlantic right whale.

As you can see, there is an overwhelming consensus of scientific data to verify that building an underwater data center is detrimental to the environment. Please reconsider allowing this real estate developer to put one in the Bay of Fundy. Thank you for your time.
